name: Chill Dog
description: Chill Dog is a rubber-guard control reached after New York by clearing the head-side grip around the neck while keeping the trapped arm isolated and the controlling knee hugged close.
summary: Chill Dog is a rubber-guard control reached after New York by clearing the head-side grip around the neck while keeping the trapped arm isolated and the controlling knee hugged close.
overview:
The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. The bottom player hugs the raised knee and has cleared the controlling arm around the head. A forearm frame and hip angle help preserve space without pulling the foot against the knee.

New York supplies the arm isolation; clearing the neck changes the controlling hand and forearm position without abandoning the knee hug. This is a guard exchange with the players facing each other. Terminology: Chill Dawg.

Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee. Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.

Keep the knee close to the torso and move from the hip. Release to guard if posture control demands knee torque or if the partner is stacked on the neck.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).
key_principles: Secure New York first: Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip.
Turn onto the hip: Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
Clear the neck: Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.
Place the inside frame: Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist.
Maintain the arm trap: Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup.
Recover when control opens: Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.

top.name: Chill Dog Top
top.description: Chill Dog top perspective: Keep the free hand available for framing while preventing the isolated elbow from being pulled further away from your torso. The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape.
top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. The bottom player hugs the raised knee and has cleared the controlling arm around the head. A forearm frame and hip angle help preserve space without pulling the foot against the knee.

Keep the free hand available for framing while preventing the isolated elbow from being pulled further away from your torso. The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape. Keep a safe base and prevent the free leg from closing high behind your head.

Recover the elbow toward your ribs only when the leg enclosure has slack, rather than jerking the shoulder. Bring the head and chest upright in stages after clearing the upper-body control. Do not drive the partner onto the neck or force the bent leg sideways to escape the control.

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: what should your free hand do while the other elbow is isolated?
flashcards.answer: Keep the free hand available for framing while preventing the isolated elbow from being pulled further away from your torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame while keeping the trapped elbow near your torso

plausible: Join the trapped hand on the mat outside their hip
Pull their ankle while extending the isolated elbow
trap: Post far behind you and lean away from the arm

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: what does their controlling hand moving around your head signal?
flashcards.answer: The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Neck clearance after the New York arm trap

plausible: The second leg joining behind the head without a hand-position change
The isolated elbow returning inside the raised knee
trap: The high leg dropping below the shoulders into ordinary closed guard

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: what should you prevent the opponent's free leg from doing?
flashcards.answer: Keep a safe base and prevent the free leg from closing high behind your head.

plausible: Resting with its foot on the floor
Returning between your hips as an ordinary frame
trap: Lowering away from your upper back

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: when should you draw the isolated elbow back toward your ribs?
flashcards.answer: Recover the elbow toward your ribs only when the leg enclosure has slack, rather than jerking the shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: When slack opens in the high-leg enclosure

plausible: While the shoulder stays fixed and the wrist is pulled
Only after forcing your head fully upright
trap: By jerking the elbow through the closed knee hug

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: what precedes restoring upright head and chest posture?
flashcards.answer: Bring the head and chest upright in stages after clearing the upper-body control.
flashcards.answer_line: Clear the upper-body enclosure in stages

plausible: Lift your chest while the trapped elbow stays extended
Push the opponent's ankle across their fixed knee
trap: Stand tall while both shoulders remain beneath the high leg

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: why should you avoid driving the bottom player onto the neck?
flashcards.answer: Do not drive the partner onto the neck or force the bent leg sideways to escape the control.
flashcards.answer_line: The stack may compress them while your arm stays trapped

plausible: Forward weight makes the knee hug slide off the elbow
Folding their hips removes the tension around your shoulder
trap: The captured arm follows your head as your weight advances

flashcards.question: Chill Dog defense: where is the opponent's main controlling leg?

bottom.overview:
The bottom player is responsible for maintaining the control. The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. The bottom player hugs the raised knee and has cleared the controlling arm around the head. flashcards.answer: Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip.
flashcards.answer_line: Their hand on the mat with your knee hugged

plausible: Their elbow framing freely between your chests
Both of your hands pulling an unsupported ankle
trap: Their posture upright above your straightened legs

flashcards.question: Chill Dog control: how do you bring the knee toward your chest without twisting it?
flashcards.answer: Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Turn your hips while supporting the raised knee

plausible: Pull the foot inward while the knee stays still
Flatten your pelvis and drag the toes across your face
trap: Extend the knee as you lift the ankle sideways

flashcards.question: Chill Dog control: what must stay connected as your arm clears around the head?
flashcards.answer: Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.
flashcards.answer_line: The high leg and isolated opposing arm

plausible: Only your foot, with the knee hug released
Only their head, with their elbow free inside
trap: Only the wrist, with the high leg slipping below the shoulder

flashcards.question: Chill Dog control: where does your forearm frame manage forward pressure?
flashcards.answer: Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist.

plausible: On the chest with your elbow flared and the wrist folded
Behind their neck while your elbow draws the head closer
trap: Low on their abdomen beneath the approaching shoulder

flashcards.question: Chill Dog control: what should you retain while choosing an omoplata or higher-leg continuation?
flashcards.answer: Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup.
flashcards.answer_line: The knee hug holding the arm isolation

plausible: A loose ankle grip with the knee unsupported
Both elbows extended away from your torso
trap: The opponent's elbow returned between your bodies

flashcards.question: Chill Dog control: the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back; what is the reset?
flashcards.answer: Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower into a comfortable guard and rebuild frames

plausible: Keep the foot fixed and twist the knee farther
Pull the escaping wrist while accepting neck compression
trap: Reach higher with the leg while your hips stay pinned

flashcards.question: Chill Dog entry: how should your body move to shorten the reach around the head?
flashcards.answer: The guard player faces the opponent from the back or hip. Move the pelvis to bring the supported knee closer; do not drag the foot across a fixed knee to create the angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Angle onto your hip with the raised knee supported

plausible: Remain flat and pull the foot inward while the knee stays behind
Lift the foot above the head before allowing the pelvis to turn
trap: Turn the chest away while leaving the bent leg pinned underneath
